newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says telecoms dupoly to last until mid-1999.
newsitem.headline: Spain says telecoms dupoly to last until mid-1999.

text.p: Spanish state telecommunications firm Retevision will enjoy a duopoly with Telefonica de Espana until mid-1999, Secretary General for Communication Jose Maria Vazquez Quintana said on Tuesday.
Retevision is preparing for a privatisation due to be completed by 2000 that would turn it into Spain's second telecommunications operator after Telefonica.

The company now focuses almost exclusively on transmitting audiovisual signals. The duopoly will last until 1999 to guarantee true competition, Vazquez Quintana told parliament's infrastructure commission.
Spain is under pressure from the European Union (EU) to open its telecommunications market to competition from cable television networks from January 1, 1998.

Vazquez Quintana said the first bids for cable licences would be awarded in March or April 1997. Under the cable law, which came into effect on September 15, operators should start transmitting cable television by summer of 1998.
He added that his department favoured a single powerful operator in the digital television market -- either Telefonica or Retevision -- to take advantage of the Hispasat satellite.
